recon.notes:
Parser config at recon: automationEnabled false, alwaysBear true, urlDiscoveryDepth 1, maxAdditionalUrls 60, no siteRole, no discoveryAllowed/BlockedPatterns. The parser was NOT in run 20260909-072307 (parserResults has no "The Bear Calendar" entry; page cache storage/pages/thebearcalendar.com is empty), so no trap carries seenInRun.
Platform confirmed by working endpoints, not markup: /feed.json (count: 66, generated_at 2026-09-08T05:15:16.069Z), /feed.ics (66 VEVENT), /feed.csv (66 rows), /feeds/ (42 .ics), /sitemap-index.xml -> /sitemap-0.xml. The whole site is a static Astro build stamped 8 Sept (sitemap lastmod 2026-09-08T05:13:42Z, header badge "SEP 8", "updated 8 Sept"), so "upcoming" is as of the build, not the request: Bear Night SEP 5 (San Diego, 2026-09-05) had already fallen off the listing.
Time semantics: feed.json start/end are ISO strings with +00:00 and tz "UTC" on 61 rows, but they are local wall-clock (CHUNK Chicago 21:00, BEEFMINCE 22:00 London). feed.ics DTSTART/DTEND are the same values as floating local times. This file records startTime/endTime as those wall-clock values and timezone as the city's IANA zone; the 5 rows with a real tz (Cruising Bears x4, Adventure Bears Panama) use that tz and their ICS local time (Panama cruise 15:00 America/New_York = feed 19:00Z).
All-day rows (25 of 66, feed all_day: true): no times; ICS DTEND;VALUE=DATE is exclusive and the page prints the inclusive range ("17–20 Sept" for DTSTART 20260917 / DTEND 20260921), endDate here is the inclusive last day. Multi-day timed rows (Club Chub Weekend 11:00 -> 14 Sept 00:00, Cádiz, Northern Exposure, Panama cruise) keep their ICS end.
Series (19 rows with rrule): feed.json/ICS start is the series anchor (often before the recon date: B BAR 2026-07-16, HONEY POT 2026-07-15), while the per-event page and its JSON-LD publish the NEXT instance ("Next / Wed 9 Sept 2026 · Wednesdays") plus an eventSchedule block (repeatFrequency P1W/P1M, byDay). startDate on series rows here is that page-published next instance; occurrences are expanded from the ICS RRULE + anchor into the window and the page's Next instance is marked origin listed. A crawl of the pages yields one dated instance per series, never the rule (scraper never writes series).
Per-event pages: exactly one schema.org Event JSON-LD block each — name, startDate/endDate (no offset), location.name + PostalAddress (locality/region/country, no street), organizer.name, image, description, offers.url (== feed ticket_url; absent when ticket_url is null), url = the aggregator page. The "Website" link (feed website_url) is a plain anchor in the page body, NOT in JSON-LD. website here = website_url, ticketUrl = ticket_url; neither is ever thebearcalendar.com. 9 rows have no organizer, 7 rows have neither outbound link (aggregator page only).
Ownership: 12 of 66 rows belong to other live parsers — BEEFMINCE x8 (organizer BEEFMINCE), CHUNK x1, Club Chub x1 (organizer Club Chub USA), BeefDip x1 (organizer BeefDip Events), Eagle LA x1 (B BAR: no organizer on the row but website_url is eaglela.com/events/b-bar/). Jackhammer Chicago, The Eagle Denver, Bears in Excess etc. are not ours. No Megawoof, Twisted Bear, Bearracuda, Furball, Cubhouse, Goldiloxx or Bear it MTL rows were listed on 2026-09-10.
City keys: 40 distinct feed city strings; 25 map to scraper-cities keys (Cathedral City -> palm-springs and WILTON MANORS -> fort-lauderdale via the configured patterns), 15 do not (city: null on those rows, listed in openQuestions). 2026-09-11: parser repointed from /events/ to feed.json (already the primary door above: same 66-row set as /events/, verified 2026-09-09; 70 rows on 2026-09-11). The feed labels wall-clock times "UTC" — the JSON-API reader verifies that against an event page and reads them as local time.

coverage.basis: feed.json: count 66 / events.length 66 (generated_at 2026-09-08T05:15:16.069Z). feed.ics: 66 VEVENTs, identical slug set (0 delta either way). feed.csv: 66 rows. /events/ (the configured url): "Showing 66 of 66 upcoming events", 66 unique /events/<slug>/ hrefs in feed order. Type feeds: 19+19+19+9+1 = 67 rows over the same 66 UIDs (belgium-bearpride-bear-folies-2026-2026 is tagged party AND pride). Organizer feeds: 36 feeds, 57 unique UIDs = 66 minus the 9 organizer-less rows. sitemap-0.xml: 387 event URLs = 66 upcoming + 321 past pages (past is not enumerated; 8 sampled, all past-dated, all still live). Published = 66 = 19 series + 47 singles; every one documented. Past listings: /events/ shows none; the 321 past pages exist only via the sitemap.

traps.label: 321 past event pages still served under /events/<slug>/ (e.g. Atlanta Bear Pride, 25-27 Apr 2025)
traps.why: sitemap-0.xml lists 387 /events/ URLs but only 66 are upcoming; the other 321 are past events that render exactly like live ones (same JSON-LD, date line, Register link) with no past marker. They are not linked from /events/, so only a sitemap or organizer-feed crawl would find them, and nothing dates them as over except the date itself.

traps.label: sitemap-0.xml (via robots.txt -> sitemap-index.xml) exposes 321 past event pages and 36 /city/<slug>/ listings
traps.why: The configured url is /events/ at urlDiscoveryDepth 1; neither the sitemap nor the /city/ pages are linked from it. The /city/ pages are filtered duplicates of the listing; the past pages are documented in the sibling trap. /sitemap.xml itself is a 404 — the real one is /sitemap-index.xml.

traps.label: /events/ links 66 event pages (plus 19 filter links ahead of them) but maxAdditionalUrls is 60
traps.why: limitAdditionalUrls() in shared-core.js keeps the first 60 discovered links in document order. Best case (only /events/<slug>/ links counted) the last 6 event pages — events[60..65], all 2027 rows — are never fetched; if the 19 /events/?type=|?city=|?range= links also count, only 41 event pages are reached. Event rows are marked expect.extracted false from position 61 on.

evidence.quote: Showing 66 of 66 upcoming events

traps.label: filter chips: /events/?type=run … ?city=london … ?range=30d (19 same-host links before the first card)
traps.why: Query-string variants of the same listing. They carry no event of their own, but they precede the event cards in the DOM and may consume the 60-link discovery budget.

traps.label: "More in United States" — 4 sibling event cards at the bottom of every event page
traps.why: Each event page ends with a rail of four other events from the same country (title, city, type, date label). A per-page extractor that reads beyond the JSON-LD could emit them as extra events wearing the host page's venue/time, or count the page as a multi-event page. Every one of them is already its own documented row.

traps.label: "66 upcoming events · 12 countries · 5 added this week · updated 8 Sept" plus the "SEP 8" date badge in the header
traps.why: Site-wide statistics and the build date, not an event. The "SEP 8" badge is the day the static site was generated (sitemap lastmod 2026-09-08), so a date sniffer would read a bogus 8 Sept event at the top of every page.

traps.label: CHUNK Chicago "TIER 1 GENERAL ADMISSION Tickets ($20)" / Western Xposure XXL "GOLD $180 (4 days), SILVER $150 (Fri-Sun), BRONZE $150 (Thu-Sat)…"
traps.why: Ticket tiers and pass types inside descriptions and the price field; they are prices of one event, not separate events or separate dates (the BRONZE Thu-Sat / SILVER Fri-Sun spans are pass windows within the 15-18 Oct run).

evidence.quote: *very limited amount of TIER 1 GENERAL ADMISSION Tickets ($20) available

traps.label: every timed event prints its wall-clock time with a "UTC" suffix, e.g. "Sat, Sep 19, 2026, 9:00 PM – 3:00 AM UTC · Chicago, IL, United States"
traps.why: Not a fake event but a fake timezone: feed.json tz is the literal string "UTC" on 61 of 66 rows and the page copies it, while the values are plainly local (9 PM Chicago, 10 PM London). JSON-LD startDate has no offset. A scraper that honours the label shifts every US/EU event by 1-9 hours. Only the 5 Cruising Bears / Adventure Bears rows carry a real tz (America/New_York, Pacific/Tahiti, Europe/Madrid, America/Los_Angeles) and print "EST".

evidence.quote: Sat, Sep 19, 2026, 9:00 PM – 3:00 AM UTC · Chicago, IL, United States

expect.note: the event itself is real and documented (chunk-chicago-2026-09-19); this trap is about the timezone label, so extraction is correct — the wall-clock must survive unshifted

openQuestions.q: 15 feed cities have no scraper-cities key, so 24 rows carry city: null: Prague, Sydney, Ottawa, Passau, Oslo, Brussels, Salt Lake City, Leipzig, Barbate, Brisbane City, Cologne, Orlando, Vienna, Gettysburg, Westfield, Maspalomas, Papeete, Barcelona. Add keys (Oslo x3, Ottawa x3, Leipzig x2, Sydney x2, Orlando x2 recur) or accept that these rows cannot be placed on a city calendar.

The site labels local wall-clock times "UTC" (feed tz "UTC", page "9:00 PM – 3:00 AM UTC", JSON-LD startDate without offset). Does the scraper's timezone step take tz from the city (correct) or from the page/feed label (shifts every US/EU event)? The 5 Cruising Bears / Adventure Bears rows DO carry a real tz and must not be treated the same way.

maxAdditionalUrls: 60 < 66 event links on /events/. Which rows drop depends on whether the 19 /events/?type=|?city=|?range= filter links (which precede the cards) count toward the budget: best case events[60..65] (six 2027 rows), worst case events[41..65]. Raise the cap (or set it null) or the 2027 cruises/IBC/Bear Carnival rows are structurally unreachable.

Series pages publish only the next instance in JSON-LD (plus an eventSchedule block); a crawl yields one dated event per series per run and the date moves every week/month. Is that the intended shape for aggregator series, or should the ICS RRULE (feed.ics) be the door for the 19 recurring rows?

BEAR POOL PARTY (Sitges, 2026-09-10, organizer Sitges Pool Party) falls inside Bears Sitges Week; not attributed to the "Bears Sitges Week" parser because the organizer is a third party. Confirm against bears-sitges-week.json once that recon lands. Likewise B BAR was attributed to "Eagle LA" from its website_url alone (no organizer on the row).

The brief cited 38 organizer feeds under /feeds/ on 2026-09-09; on 2026-09-10 the index lists 36 while the event count is unchanged at 66. Organizer feeds appear to be derived from the current organizer set, so the count drifts with the listing.

Past event pages (321) are still served 200 with full JSON-LD and no past marker, and the static build is a day or more behind (Bear Night SEP 5 dropped from the listing while its page lives on). If a future config adds sitemap discovery or allowPastEvents, every one of those pages will look live.
